speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: asked the Minister for Transport what are the transportation infrastructure plans to support the build-up of Tuas Mega Port and increased business activities in Tuas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This has brought about significant time savings for commuters travelling to the Tuas area.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: I understand that in 2019, an assessment was made that the Tuas South MRT Line has insufficient ridership to support a line there.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Three years down the road, based on current estimates, will there be an update for this assessment?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is an issue which we will continue to monitor.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I have explained in this House previously that the extension of the MRT network will depend on the demand for public transport services.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this is not going to be dependent only on the workers who are going to PSA, but also on the surrounding industrial area where we are planning to build up some manufacturing capabilities in the vicinity of the port.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, depending on the developments and also depending on the demand for public transport services, the need to invest additional amount of resources to extend the MRT can then be made based on this more holistic and complete picture.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would just like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether there are any plans to expand the road network or to increase the capacity of current expressways or roads leading to Tuas and the Tuas Mega Port area, specifically, for road transport and logistical purposes?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And if so, when will these constructions be taken?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As Mr Tan pointed out, we want to make sure that for the container trucks and also other vehicles that are travelling to and from the port, there will be sufficient capacity to cater to this requirement.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The development of the port will not happen in one phase but over a period of time; demand will build up.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And therefore, the development of the road infrastructure to support port operations would also have to be reviewed in tandem with how we scale up the operations of Tuas Port.
